h: Food, Fields and the Orwell Estuary
p: Jimmy's Farm is at Wherstead, on the southern edge of Ipswich close to the River Orwell. The farm first came to national attention through the BBC series Jimmy's Farm, which followed Jimmy Doherty as he set up his rare-breed pig farm here, and he's been a familiar face on food and farming telly ever since. That food-first approach shows. Plenty of visitors come as much for the farm shop and restaurant as for the animals, which makes it a handy place to meet friends or grandparents who might not be quite as excited by a meerkat as the kids are.

Go with a loose plan rather than a tight schedule. Children can spend ages on the farm side alone, feeding time and fence-leaning included, before you even get to the wilder animals. Comfy boots or wellies help, especially after rain, and a coat is wise because the Suffolk breeze can be keen even on a bright day.

The surrounding area is lovely for a follow-up. Alton Water, a reservoir a few miles south, has walking and cycling routes all the way round, plus water sports in season. Pin Mill, on the south bank of the Orwell, is a tiny riverside hamlet with old sailing barges and a much-loved pub on the shore. On the way back you'll likely cross under or over the Orwell Bridge, a striking landmark on the A14. Felixstowe's seafront and gardens are within easy reach too, if the kids are still shouting for a beach.
